deliverables: Cardano hardware-wallet maintenance and compatibility assurance
Maintenance of supporting interoperability libraries and cardano-hw-cli
Support for integration paths involving externally maintained components where shared hardware-wallet flows intersect
Vendor-required product or security audits where firmware or app changes trigger them
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund 12 months of Hardware Wallet Maintenance 2026, covering Ledger and Trezor compatibility updates, interoperability libraries, cardano-hw-cli, developer support, integration-path support, and vendor-required product or security audits.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,310,960 ADA, consisting of 1,272,777 ADA for Cardano Hardware Wallet Maintenance & Compatibility Assurance and 38,183 ADA for an Intersect Budget Administration fee.
The work is described as a continuity proposal for an already-proven Cardano access layer rather than a new wallet product.
The proposer states that continuous maintenance is needed because Cardano protocol evolution, vendor firmware and app release cycles, and wallet and dApp integration demand create compatibility risk.

The proposer states that the scope is limited to hardware-wallet compatibility, tooling, supporting libraries, release support, and vendor-required assurance, and does not duplicate broader core-node, ledger, or general infrastructure maintenance budgets.
The proposal states that it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposer claims the requested withdrawal does not, at the time of submission, individually or in aggregate breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
The proposal says withdrawn funds will be administered through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts using one Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract.

The proposal identifies the Oversight Committee as Sundae Labs, Cardano Foundation, Dquadrant, NMKR, Sundial, and Eternl, with specified multisignature approvals for fund, disburse, pause, sweep, and reorganize actions.

The proposer states that audit and oversight costs are included within the proposal overhead and that independent oversight will include reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.

The document discloses prior treasury and Catalyst funding related to hardware wallets, Ledger app work, Plutus enhancement, security, token, and developer ecosystem projects through listed governance-action and Project Catalyst links.

summary: The document requests 1,310,960 ADA for a 2026 hardware-wallet maintenance program administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts, with claimed Hydra budget-process approval, NCL compliance, oversight controls, and disclosed related prior funding.
